Replay

Immutable 2D polygon meshes

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

mesh2_polygon(instance, points) triangulates a simple polygon and installs an untextured ArrayMesh on a Godot MeshInstance2D. It accepts 3–4096 finite vertices. Failure leaves the previous mesh in place. The caller owns the input packed array; the node owns the resulting mesh through Godot's normal reference counting. Replacing the mesh releases the node's reference to its previous resource.

Create geometry when its shape changes. Animate Node2D.transform, visibility, and CanvasItem.self_modulate for placement, scaling and tint. Reuse a canonical unit shape when an affine transform describes the animation. Callers can also share the resulting immutable mesh using Godot's ordinary mesh resource references. The helper does not introduce global caches, simulation state or network identity.

Odin
node := gd.new_mesh_instance2d()
points := gd.new_packed_vector2_array()
for point in ([3]gd.Vector2{{0, 0}, {20, 0}, {0, 20}}) {
    gd.packed_vector2_array_append(&points, point)
}
ok := scenegd.mesh2_polygon(node, points)
gd.free_packed_vector2_array(points)
if ok {
    gd.add_child(parent, node)
    gd.canvas_item_set_self_modulate(node, {1, 0.8, 0.2, 0.5})
} else {
    gdext.object_destroy(node)
}

This is useful with Godot 4.7.1's compatibility web renderer. Its Polygon2D redraw path can update an existing index buffer through a vertex-buffer target, including when color, visibility or viewport changes cause redraw. Immutable mesh instances avoid that update path. They also avoid repeated triangulation/uploads when only pose or color changes. See the reproduction and validation.

For observation tools, Mesh.surface_get_arrays can read back GPU buffers. Cache immutable geometry by mesh resource identity instead of performing that readback on every frame. Instance pose/tint remain separately observable and mutable.
